title: Is-This-a-Bot Test Line
one_liner: Runs scripted test calls and chats on a business's AI receptionist or avatar to check disclosure, memory and sales pressure.
speaker: Peter Diamandis
context: After a viral clip of an AI avatar recognising itself in a mirror, Peter asked when an AI must say it is an AI, who owns what it remembers, and whether these faces will be used to persuade or sell.
customer: US small businesses using AI voice receptionists or chat avatars (dental and medical front desks, home-services firms, car dealerships), plus the agencies that install those agents for them
problem: Owners switch on an AI agent and never check how it answers 'am I talking to a bot?', what it says it remembers about callers, or how hard it pushes upsells. They find out when a customer complains or posts a recording.
revenue_model: Fixed fee of about $400 per test pass (25 scripted probes across voice and chat) with a scored report, plus about $99 a month for a re-test after each agent or vendor update (estimate). Agencies get a white-label bulk rate.
why_now: Avatar agents are now lifelike enough that a mirror-test demo drew nearly 24 million views and strong 'skin crawl' reactions. The hosts raised disclosure, memory ownership and persuasion as open questions as these agents spread.
first_steps: Write a 25-question probe script (bot disclosure, memory, data deletion, upsell pressure, escalation to a human) and run it on 5 public AI receptionist demo lines
Turn one run into a sample scored report and send it to 20 local agencies that install AI receptionists
Offer 3 free test passes to small businesses in exchange for a testimonial and permission to publish an anonymised result
cost_to_start: About 1–2 weeks and under $200 for a phone number, call recording and a simple report template (estimate).
competition: Enterprise conversational-AI QA and red-team platforms exist. A cheap, fixed-fee behaviour check for small businesses appears thin (unverified).
risks: Customers may expect a legal compliance certificate, so the reports must be framed as behaviour tests, not legal advice. Agent vendors may add their own built-in tests. Each pass is low-ticket, so the business depends on agency volume.

tool.title: Bot Honesty Scorecard
tool.one_liner: Builds a test script for your AI agent and scores a pasted transcript on disclosure, memory and pressure tactics.
tool.demo: The owner picks their business type and channel (phone or chat) and gets a ready-to-run list of probe questions. After running them, they paste the transcript and get a score per category (admits it is AI, explains memory, offers a human, avoids pressure), with the quoted lines that caused each flag. Rule-based scoring works with no key. A visitor-pasted AI key adds a richer written review.
tool.data_plan: The customer's own transcript and business details. Probe questions come from a bundled list built from the episode's four questions. No external data.
acceptance: Choosing 'dental clinic' and 'phone' produces a numbered probe script of at least 15 questions grouped under disclosure, memory, human hand-off and sales pressure
Pasting the bundled example transcript and pressing Score shows a 0–100 score per category and highlights the transcript lines that triggered each flag
With no API key, an example mode fills every report section and labels it 'Example – rule-based scoring'
The page states that the report is a behaviour test, not legal or compliance advice
The scorecard can be printed or saved as a single-page PDF via the browser, and the layout stacks into one column on a phone
